extracted.intended_audience: faculty, staff, and administrators at two-year (community) colleges seeking external grant funding
extracted.subtask_short: writing grant proposals for two-year colleges
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, preparing, and submitting external grant proposals from two-year colleges, covering how to find funding sources, organize the proposal process, and write required sections (summary, narrative, budget, appendices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project planning — identify institutional need and develop idea
rubrics_metrics.description: First, identify the institution's need and develop an idea of how the need can be met. The idea should be practical and of real importance in strengthening education at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the idea with the individuals who will be involved in implementing the project. If sufficient interest is expressed and support seems to be forthcoming from the administration and faculty, locate a source of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding appropriate funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding a possible funding source is primarily a process of identifying a foundation or agency that has a history of funding projects in the same subject area or with a similar purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult your college or district development officer and your state education agency. Carefully examine each program's pamphlet or booklet for areas of interest and requirements; determine whether the project's scope and requirements match the funder's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inquiry (brief project description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Send a brief (no more than two pages long) description of the project, including the objectives, to agencies and foundations which seem to be interested in similar projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A program representative can determine whether the project is appropriate; keep the inquiry concise and focused on objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funding-information resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult specialized resources (e.g., Foundation Center, Grant Information System, Grantsmanship Center, NCRD, Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance, Chronicle of Higher Education) to locate potential funders and learn deadlines and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources provide directories, searchable catalogs, program objectives, eligibility requirements, application processes, and deadline listings useful for targeting funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize the proposal writing process with a timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline with deadlines for each section of the proposal should be developed to ensure that all requirements are met by the time the proposal is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circulate deadlines to everyone involved and keep in touch with the agency/foundation representative to resolve problems or questions quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include common proposal features
rubrics_metrics.description: Most proposals have these common features: (1) a project summary, (2) a narrative, (3) a budget statement and justification, and (4) appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that requirements differ by funder; follow the funder's specified formats and length limits for these sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project summary — clear, precise, complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The project summary, as well as the rest of the proposal, should be written in clear, precise language without the use of obscuring jargon. An accurate and complete description of the project objectives and procedures should be given with as much detail as possible in the length specified in the proposal guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep within the funder's length limits while providing sufficient detail to convey objectives and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — address key components
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative usually addresses: 1) a statement of the problem, 2) a review of the literature, 3) the project objectives, 4) the procedures, 5) the significance, 6) the evaluation method, 7) dissemination, 8) staff qualifications, and 9) the schedule of activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each of these points is clearly and specifically developed so reviewers can judge need, approach, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description of the topic addressed and an explanation of both the institutional and societal needs for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use relevant information about the institution to demonstrate that the project is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The literature review both supports the need for the project and shows evidence that the project planners have made a detailed investigation of prior attempts to meet the need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use databases such as ERIC to provide a comprehensive view of documents and prior work, including final reports of federally funded projects and government research reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives — realistic and linked to problem
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of what the project will accomplish should be provided in the narrative. These objectives should be realistic and follow directly from the statement of the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State measurable or clear objectives that address the identified needs; avoid overly ambitious or vague goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures — detailed methods and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the procedures to be followed in conducting the project and the reasons for choosing these procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the population involved, the methods used, and the materials developed; provide sufficient detail so reviewers understand how the project will be implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — contribution and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a statement of what the project will add to existing knowledge or how the project will improve current practices to emphasize the importance of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight potential broader impacts and relevance beyond the originating institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — external, formative and summative
rubrics_metrics.description: Most funding sources require some form of evaluation, usually external, to objectively determine what the project achieved and to ensure that any recommendations follow from what actually took place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the evaluation process and include both formative and summative components; identify external evaluators either generally or, if possible, by name and title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination — demonstrate wider usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the process of disseminating the project findings or outcomes to demonstrate the project's usefulness outside the originating institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a statement that a description of the project or the final project report will be submitted to ERIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff qualifications — document expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a paragraph for each principal staff member detailing his or her educational background and relevant experience or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place complete vitae of staff members in the appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of activities — comprehensive timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently, the funding source requires the completion of a comprehensive schedule form showing an exact deadline for the accomplishment of each part of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a form is not provided by the funder, include a detailed timeline in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget statement and justification — accurate and realistic
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget should be accurate and realistic. Most funding sources have a detailed budget form with spaces for each category of expense that should be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address usual categories (personnel including benefits; equipment; supplies; travel; consultant fees; other expenses such as utilities, computer time, publication; indirect costs/overhead). Explain fully how estimates were made for each category; credibility of the budget adds authority to the proposal. Find out the college's overhead rate if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices — include supportive but concise materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The appendices should contain any additional supporting material, such as the vitae of key personnel, background material on the institution, and letters of recommendation from community members or involved individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to double the size of proposals with supporting material; include only necessary documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and internal review before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: After the proposal is completed, an individual who has been closely involved in the planning process should read over the entire proposal carefully checking for consistency and continuity throughout the sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that all the funding agency's and the college's requirements have been met; have the college's development office review if necessary before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Following up after non-funding — obtain evaluators' comments and revise
rubrics_metrics.description: Many agencies and foundations will release a copy of the evaluators' comments to the submitters of unsuccessful proposals. These comments can provide valuable feedback and suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find out whether the proposal can be revised and resubmitted; if so, revise and plan for next year's competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match proposal to funder's scope and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully examine the scope of concern and requirements of the possible sources of funds to determine fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funder pamphlets and program descriptions; a program representative can help determine appropriateness and avoid wasted effort on mismatched submissions.
